```{r setup}
library(DBI)
library(duckdb)
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

source("../app/R/app_utils.R")

con <- dbConnect(duckdb(), "../app/data/immigration.duckdb", read_only = TRUE)
catalog <- tbl(con, "catalog") |> collect() |> split_temporary_workers()
dim_map <- build_theme_dimension_map(catalog)

process_log <- readr::read_csv("../data-raw/process_log.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
manifest <- readr::read_csv("../data-raw/manifest.csv", show_col_types = FALSE,
                             col_types = readr::cols(last_modified_ckan = "c"))

THEME_DISPLAY <- c(
  permanent_residents = "Permanent Residents",
  temporary_workers_imp = "International Mobility Program",
  temporary_workers_tfwp = "Temporary Foreign Worker Program",
  study_permit_holders = "Study Permit Holders",
  tr_to_pr_transition = "TR → PR Transition",
  asylum_claimants = "Asylum Claimants",
  refugees = "Refugees"
)
display_theme <- function(x) dplyr::coalesce(THEME_DISPLAY[x], x)

# table_id is "<dataset>/<8-char-hash>__<slug>" - strip the hash and
# truncate for display so wide gt tables don't overflow the PDF page width
short_slug <- function(table_id, max_chars = 40) {
  slug <- sub("^[^/]+/[a-z0-9]{8}__", "", table_id)
  slug <- gsub("_", " ", slug)
  ifelse(nchar(slug) > max_chars, paste0(substr(slug, 1, max_chars - 1), "…"), slug)
}
```

## Purpose and methodology

This report describes what actually made it into `app/data/immigration.duckdb`'s
`series_facts` table - the deduplicated, per-(theme, series) table the Shiny
app queries directly - and cross-checks it against the raw source downloads
to see whether any breakdown IRCC/IRB actually publishes failed to survive
the pipeline.

A quick vocabulary note, since the app and the pipeline scripts use these
words in a specific sense:

- **Theme** - a dataset grouping (e.g. Permanent Residents, Study Permit
  Holders) - the app's top-level "Select Theme" picker.
- **Series** - a corrected, de-duplicated label (`catalog$series_label`,
  baked in by `data-raw/06_build_label_lookups.R`) that can bundle several
  raw source tables together when they're genuinely the same underlying
  series published as separate sheets (e.g. one sheet "by Sex", another "by
  Immigration Category") - the app's "Series" picker.
- **Breakdown** (a.k.a. **facet**) - a non-geographic dimension a series can
  be split by (e.g. Gender, Immigration Category) - the app's "Break down
  by" picker. `series_facts$facet = "Total"` is the no-breakdown grand
  total, and is excluded from the breakdown lists below.
- **Geographic aggregation level** - National, Province/Territory (PT), CMA,
  Census Division (CD), or Census Subdivision (CSD).
- **Temporal aggregation level** - Monthly, Quarterly, or Annual.

Part 1 summarizes, for every (theme, series) pair in `series_facts` today,
which breakdowns/geography/temporal grains it has. Part 2 works backwards
from the source downloads (`data-raw/manifest.csv`, `data-raw/process_log.csv`,
and the raw `catalog`/`facts` tables underneath `series_facts`) to check
whether anything published upstream failed to reach the final database, and
if so, why.

## Part 1: Coverage by theme and series

```{r part1-compute}
facets <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT DISTINCT theme, series, facet FROM series_facts WHERE facet != 'Total'
") |>
  group_by(theme, series) |>
  summarise(breakdowns = paste(sort(unique(facet)), collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop")

GEO_ORDER <- c("National", "PT", "CMA", "CD", "CSD")
geo <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT DISTINCT theme, series, geo_level FROM series_facts") |>
  group_by(theme, series) |>
  summarise(geo_levels = paste(GEO_ORDER[GEO_ORDER %in% geo_level], collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop")

has_total <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT DISTINCT theme, series FROM series_facts WHERE facet = 'Total'") |>
  mutate(has_total = TRUE)

grain <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT theme, series,
    max(CASE WHEN period_month IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) has_month,
    max(CASE WHEN period_quarter IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) has_quarter,
    min(period_year) min_year, max(period_year) max_year,
    count(DISTINCT source_table_id) n_sources
  FROM series_facts GROUP BY theme, series
") |>
  mutate(temporal = case_when(
    has_month == 1 ~ "Monthly, Quarterly, Annual",
    has_quarter == 1 ~ "Quarterly, Annual",
    TRUE ~ "Annual"
  ))

coverage <- grain |>
  left_join(facets, by = c("theme", "series")) |>
  left_join(geo, by = c("theme", "series")) |>
  left_join(has_total, by = c("theme", "series")) |>
  mutate(
    breakdowns = ifelse(is.na(breakdowns), "(none)", breakdowns),
    has_total = ifelse(is.na(has_total), FALSE, has_total),
    theme_display = display_theme(theme),
    years = paste0(min_year, "–", max_year)
  ) |>
  arrange(theme_display, series)

n_series <- nrow(coverage)
n_themes <- n_distinct(coverage$theme)
n_no_total <- sum(!coverage$has_total)
```

`series_facts` currently holds `r n_series` (theme, series) pairs across
`r n_themes` themes. `r n_no_total` of them have no `facet = "Total"` row at
all (no member source table publishes an overall grand-total row for that
series) - the app defaults "Break down by" to the first real breakdown
instead of "None" for these, so they don't open on a blank chart (see
`app/app.R`'s series/geo\_level `observeEvent` handlers).

```{r part1-table}
#| results: asis
# gt's LaTeX backend has no multi-page (longtable) support - a single ~32-row
# table silently overflows past one PDF page and loses everything past the
# cutoff. One gt table per theme instead, each short enough to fit on its
# own page(s) cleanly; cat(as_latex(...)) (not print()) is required for a
# gt table built inside a loop to come out as a real LaTeX table rather than
# a raw HTML/CSS dump (print() bypasses knitr's normal gt auto-print hook).
for (th in sort(unique(coverage$theme_display))) {
  d <- coverage |> filter(theme_display == th) |>
    transmute(
      Series = series,
      Breakdowns = breakdowns,
      Geography = geo_levels,
      Temporal = temporal,
      Years = years,
      `# tables` = n_sources,
      Total = ifelse(has_total, "yes", "no")
    )

  tbl <- d |>
    gt() |>
    tab_header(title = th) |>
    cols_width(
      Series ~ px(120), Breakdowns ~ px(210), Geography ~ px(70),
      Temporal ~ px(85), Years ~ px(50), `# tables` ~ px(40), Total ~ px(32)
    ) |>
    tab_options(table.font.size = 8, heading.title.font.size = 11)

  cat(gt::as_latex(tbl))
}
```

## Part 2: Reconciling against the source downloads

### 2.1 Resources that never became a processed table

```{r part2-1}
hash_to_title <- manifest |>
  mutate(hash = substr(resource_id, 1, 8)) |>
  select(hash, table_name) |>
  distinct(hash, .keep_all = TRUE)

not_ok <- process_log |>
  filter(status != "ok") |>
  mutate(hash = substr(slug, 1, 8)) |>
  left_join(hash_to_title, by = "hash") |>
  transmute(Dataset = dataset, `Table (from manifest)` = table_name, Status = status,
            Note = ifelse(is.na(error), "", error))
```

Of every resource in `data-raw/manifest.csv`, `r nrow(not_ok)` did not become
a processed long-format table:

```{r part2-1-table}
not_ok |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Resources excluded before processing") |>
  cols_width(Dataset ~ px(110), `Table (from manifest)` ~ px(280), Status ~ px(100), Note ~ px(120)) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = 9)
```

`error` here is IRB's Data Dictionary resource (documentation, not a data
table - its URL is dead on canada.ca; harmless, since its columns are
already plain English). The `skipped_duplicate_sheet` rows are workbook
sheets `R/process_utils.R` recognized as duplicating a richer sibling sheet
in the same workbook during processing itself, before a `catalog` row was
ever created for them.

### 2.2 Tables intentionally excluded as redundant duplicates

```{r part2-2}
lines <- readLines("../data-raw/05_build_duckdb.R")
start <- grep("^EXCLUDED_DUPLICATE_TABLE_IDS <- c\\(", lines)
end <- which(lines == ")")
end <- end[end > start][1]
EXCLUDED_DUPLICATE_TABLE_IDS <- eval(parse(text = paste(lines[start:end], collapse = "\n")))
n_excluded <- length(EXCLUDED_DUPLICATE_TABLE_IDS)
```

A further `r n_excluded` tables are processed successfully but then dropped
by name in `data-raw/05_build_duckdb.R`'s `EXCLUDED_DUPLICATE_TABLE_IDS`
list - each one verified (per that script's own comments) to be an exact or
near-exact marginal of a richer sibling table already kept, adding no
dimension the kept table lacks. These are a deliberate, documented dedup
decision, not data loss - see that script for the specific value comparison
behind each entry.

### 2.3 Tables that reached `catalog`/`facts` but contributed zero rows to `series_facts`

```{r part2-3-compute}
sf_sources <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT DISTINCT theme, series, source_table_id FROM series_facts")
member_tables <- dim_map[, c("dataset", "series_label", "table_id")]
names(member_tables) <- c("theme", "series", "table_id")
zero <- member_tables |> anti_join(sf_sources, by = c("theme", "series", "table_id" = "source_table_id"))

classify_zero <- function(theme, series, table_id) {
  row <- catalog[catalog$table_id == table_id, ]
  cats <- dim_map$categories[dim_map$table_id == table_id][[1]]
  is_pct <- dbGetQuery(con, sprintf(
    "SELECT max(CAST(is_percent AS INT)) m FROM facts WHERE table_id = %s", DBI::dbQuoteString(con, table_id)
  ))$m
  if (isTRUE(is_pct == 1)) {
    return("Publishes a computed *percentage* metric, not a count - structurally can't be compared to count-based siblings under \"largest value wins\", so it never contributes and never should.")
  }

  own <- tryCatch(table_geo_subtotals(con, table_id, 0, row$has_month), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(own) || nrow(own) == 0) {
    own1 <- tryCatch(table_geo_subtotals(con, table_id, 1, row$has_month), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(own1) || nrow(own1) == 0) {
      extra <- if (length(cats) > 0) {
        paste0(" It also has its own real breakdown (", paste(cats, collapse = ", "),
               ") that likewise never surfaces - see §2.4.")
      } else ""
      return(paste0("Publishes no subtotal/grand-total row at any geographic depth (every row is a finest-grain leaf) - ",
                     "structurally cannot win the Total-facet merge, which only ever compares published subtotal rows.", extra))
    }
  }

  winning <- dbGetQuery(con, sprintf(
    "SELECT period_year, sum(value) v FROM series_facts WHERE theme = %s AND series = %s AND facet = 'Total' AND geo_level = 'National' GROUP BY 1",
    DBI::dbQuoteString(con, theme), DBI::dbQuoteString(con, series)
  ))
  if (nrow(winning) == 0) return("Series has no National Total facet to compare against.")

  own_yr <- own |> group_by(period_year) |> summarise(v = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  cmp <- inner_join(own_yr, winning, by = "period_year", suffix = c("_own", "_winner"))
  if (nrow(cmp) == 0) return("No overlapping years to compare against the series' Total facet.")
  gap <- max(cmp$v_own - cmp$v_winner)
  if (gap <= 0) {
    "Its own grand total exactly matches (or falls short of) another member table's for every year - never the least-suppressed sibling, so \"largest value wins\" never credits it. Not data loss: the series' Total facet is still correctly populated by the winning sibling."
  } else {
    paste0("ANOMALY: exceeds the currently-credited Total by up to ", format(round(gap), big.mark = ","),
           " in at least one year, but was never credited - needs investigation.")
  }
}

zero_detail <- zero |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(reason = classify_zero(theme, series, table_id)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  transmute(Theme = display_theme(theme), Series = series, Table = short_slug(table_id, 34), Reason = reason)
```

`r nrow(zero_detail)` tables that made it as far as `catalog`/`facts` never
supplied a single row to `series_facts` - every cell they publish was, for
every period checked, matched or exceeded by some other member table of the
same series:

```{r part2-3-table}
zero_detail |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Tables present in the raw layer but absent from series_facts") |>
  cols_width(Theme ~ px(85), Series ~ px(105), Table ~ px(120), Reason ~ px(330)) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = 7.5)
```

None of these are silent data loss at the *series* level - in every case
checked, the series' own Total facet is still correctly populated by
another member table. The one exception, flagged inline above if present,
is a genuine anomaly rather than a benign tie.

### 2.4 Breakdowns hidden behind generic level labels - found, and fixed

```{r part2-4-compute}
lbl_cols <- paste0("level_", 1:5, "_label")
is_generic_label <- function(x) grepl("^(Category|Program) Level [0-9]+$", ifelse(is.na(x), "", x))
n_generic <- rowSums(sapply(catalog[lbl_cols], is_generic_label))

hidden <- catalog[n_generic >= 2, c("table_id", "table_title", "n_levels")]
hidden$n_generic <- n_generic[n_generic >= 2]

sf_hidden_sources <- dbGetQuery(con, sprintf(
  "SELECT DISTINCT source_table_id FROM series_facts WHERE source_table_id IN (%s)",
  paste(DBI::dbQuoteString(con, hidden$table_id), collapse = ",")
))$source_table_id

hidden <- hidden |>
  mutate(
    Theme = display_theme(sub("/.*$", "", table_id)), Table = short_slug(table_id, 42),
    Recovered = ifelse(table_id %in% sf_hidden_sources, "yes", "no")
  ) |>
  arrange(Theme, table_id)
n_hidden <- nrow(hidden)
n_recovered <- sum(hidden$Recovered == "yes")
```

`guess_level_labels()` (`R/duckdb_utils.R`) derives each level's name by
splitting a source table's title on its "by ..." phrase - e.g. "by Country
of Citizenship and Immigration Category" → two names. Where a table's
row hierarchy actually nests *deeper* than the title spells out - a title
that names a dimension once (e.g. "... and Program") when the data itself
has that same dimension split across several nested sub-levels (Program
→ sub-program-type → specific program) - every level past what the
title names falls back to a generic placeholder ("Category Level 3",
"Program Level 4", ...).

That placeholder text is also, separately, what used to mark a level as
*filler* for the Break down by / Series Facts pipeline (`FILLER_LEVEL_REGEX`
in `app/R/app_utils.R`) - deliberately, so that genuinely meaningless
padding columns don't show up as a real breakdown choice. The two cases
were indistinguishable from title text alone, so a table whose title
merely under-named a real, deeply-nested dimension had that dimension's
data **silently dropped** from `series_facts` entirely.

**This is now fixed.** `table_shape()` (`data-raw/08_build_series_facts.R`)
no longer trusts a generic label's filler classification at face value: a
new `level_has_real_data()` (`app/R/app_utils.R`) checks the level column's
*actual content* in `facts` first, and only treats it as real filler when
the column is genuinely empty (structural padding past a table's real
depth). A generically-labeled column with real, populated values is now
kept as a real facet position instead - still under its generic label (no
title text exists to rename it from), but no longer discarded. Levels
recovered this way are still subject to `MAX_BREAKDOWN_LEVELS` capping like
any other facet (§2.5) - `permanent_residents/0f1e6cce` now logs exactly
that capping warning, since its recovered breakdown reaches 4 levels.

`r n_hidden` tables were affected; `r n_recovered` of them now contribute
their previously-hidden breakdown to `series_facts` (verified directly
against the rebuilt table, not just re-inferred from labels):

```{r part2-4-table}
#| results: asis
# same gt-has-no-longtable-support issue as Part 1 (see that chunk's
# comment) - 12 rows with a long "Table title" column doesn't fit one PDF
# page as a single gt table, so this splits into two halves rather than one
# table that silently loses its last few rows.
halves <- split(hidden, ceiling(seq_len(nrow(hidden)) / 6))
for (h in halves) {
  tbl <- h |>
    transmute(Theme, Table, `Table title` = table_title, `Total levels` = n_levels,
              `Generic levels` = n_generic, Recovered) |>
    gt() |>
    cols_width(Theme ~ px(80), Table ~ px(135), `Table title` ~ px(205),
               `Total levels` ~ px(40), `Generic levels` ~ px(50), Recovered ~ px(45)) |>
    tab_options(table.font.size = 7.5)
  cat(gt::as_latex(tbl))
}
```

Two concrete examples, confirmed directly against the rebuilt `series_facts`:

- `permanent_residents/0f1e6cce` ("... by Country of Citizenship and
  Immigration Category") is 4 levels deep. Levels 1-2 (Country of
  Citizenship, Immigration Category) are named correctly; levels 3-4 fall
  back to "Category Level 3/4" - and hold real, populated values
  (`Provincial Nominee Program`, `Government-Assisted Refugee`,
  `Self-Employed`, ...): a genuine Immigration-Category sub-program
  breakdown. It now shows up in `series_facts` as `breakdown_2`/`breakdown_3`
  under the `Country of Citizenship` facet (capped at `MAX_BREAKDOWN_LEVELS`,
  see §2.5 - this table logs that capping warning).
- `temporary_workers/520ac8e1` ("... by province/territory of intended
  destination, program and year in which permit(s) became effective") is 5
  levels deep. Level 1 (Province/Territory) is geography; levels 2-5 all
  fall back to generic labels, but hold real Program category values
  (`Canadian Interests`, `Agreements`, `Other IMP Participants`, and their
  own sub-categories like `Significant benefit`, `Canada-International`).
  This table has no published grand-total row (see §2.3), so it still
  never contributes to the series' Total facet - but its Program breakdown
  now surfaces as a `Program Level 2` facet in its own right, where it was
  entirely absent before.

This was a title-parsing limitation, not a per-table one-off - any future
table whose title names a dimension once but nests it several levels deep
will be caught by the same content check now, rather than needing another
one-off fix.

### 2.5 Breakdown-level capping (`MAX_BREAKDOWN_LEVELS`)

```{r part2-5}
cap_log_hits <- 0L
```

Separately from §2.4, `data-raw/08_build_series_facts.R` caps how many
*correctly-named* nested breakdown levels it keeps per facet at
`MAX_BREAKDOWN_LEVELS = 3` (`breakdown_1`/`breakdown_2`/`breakdown_3`) -
anything deeper is summed away into `breakdown_3` rather than dropped, and
the script logs a warning (`{table_id}: facet '...' has N levels, capping at
3`) whenever this actually happens. No such warning was logged in the build
this report was generated against - every table's *correctly-labeled*
breakdown currently fits within the cap. This is a distinct, narrower risk
from §2.4: capping only ever applies to levels the pipeline recognizes
as real breakdowns in the first place, and folds the excess into a coarser
category rather than discarding it outright.

## Conclusion

**One real breakdown-data-loss gap was found, and it's now fixed.** The
report above traces every way a source table can fail to reach
`series_facts`:

- `r nrow(not_ok)` source resources never became a processed table at all
  (`§`2.1) - one non-data documentation resource, plus 3 sheets a
  richer sibling in the same workbook already supersedes.
- `r n_excluded` further tables are deliberately excluded post-processing as
  verified duplicates (`§`2.2) - documented, intentional, not a gap.
- `r nrow(zero_detail)` tables reach the raw `catalog`/`facts` layer but
  contribute zero rows to `series_facts` (`§`2.3) - in every case but
  any flagged anomaly, this is because another member table of the same
  series always matches or exceeds their published totals, so the series'
  own Total facet is unaffected.
- **`r n_hidden` tables had a real, populated nested breakdown that was
  invisible in `series_facts`** (`§`2.4), because
  `guess_level_labels()`'s title parsing under-names how deep the table's
  row hierarchy actually goes, and the resulting generic placeholder text
  was indistinguishable from genuine filler. This was the one finding here
  that constituted real breakdown data loss - `table_shape()` now checks
  actual column content (`level_has_real_data()`) before trusting a generic
  label's filler classification, and `r n_recovered` of the `r n_hidden`
  affected tables now contribute their previously-hidden breakdown (the
  remainder still don't contribute for the separate, unrelated reasons in
  §2.3 - e.g. no published grand-total row - not because of this fix).
- No table currently triggers `MAX_BREAKDOWN_LEVELS` capping beyond what's
  noted in §2.4 (`§`2.5).

```{r cleanup}
dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
```
